subject: Post-demo: technical qualification & model scorecard
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: technical qualification & model scorecard

Hi Ethan — great meeting today, thanks for the time. 

Summary from our side and suggested next steps: 

- Quick recap: you showed the core search-to-answer workflow and the high-value UX constraints (95th pctile latency targets ~300ms, golden-path accuracy metric = F1 on entity extraction + hallucination score).
- Preliminary model shortlist (attached scorecard): small/high-throughput candidate, mid-size quality-first, and a distill variant for cheap batch jobs. See attached CSV for the numeric tradeoffs.

Main tradeoffs we flagged during the demo:
- Latency vs. quality: lowest-latency model is ~3-5x cheaper per token but drops on rare-entity recall (we saw 6-8% drop on your holdout).
- Tokenization & prompt length: your average prompt is ~450 tokens; that favors models with efficient KV cache behavior.
- Regression risk: we recommend running the provided prompt_set_v2 on every release. We'll wire that into CI so you get automatic quality regression alerts.

Concrete asks / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm the data retention & redaction requirement for PII? (Marissa, looping you for SOC/PII note.)
2) We'll share an evaluation pack (attached prompts + benchmark CSV) and a short recording from today. Please run the scorecard against your internal sample and tell us which metric you prioritize (latency threshold vs. recall).
3) If acceptable, propose a 2-week POC: run 3 model variants on a subset of traffic (10%) with our canary routing so we can measure production-like latencies.

Attachments: finlytics_benchmark_results_v1.csv (scorecard), finlytics_prompt_set_v2.txt, demo_recording_20261004.mp4

Thanks — I'll follow up with a proposed POC plan once you confirm retention and prioritized metric.

—Sergio

From: Ethan Morris <ethan@finlytics.com>

Cc: Finlytics Solutions Team <solutions@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: technical qualification & model scorecard

Thanks Sergio — useful recap. A few clarifying questions from the Finlytics engineering team: 

1) On the "distill" variant: what quantization level did you use for the throughput numbers? Are those int8 or int4 figures?
2) For the mid-size model you recommend, can you share a sample prompt/response pair against our prompt_set_v2? We saw the CSV but not the raw outputs.
3) For PII, we need redaction at ingest and a 90-day retention window (logs only). Will that block the POC?

Also, we're sensitive to surprises around hallucination on financial tickers — can we add a ticker-specific slice to the scorecard? I'll attach a short list of examples in a follow-up.

—Ethan
Ethan Morris | Head of Product
Finlytics
ethan@finlytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan@finlytics.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: technical qualification & model scorecard

Ethan — quick answers inline and a sample I pasted below.

1) Quantization: the distill numbers in the CSV assume int8 kernels on A100/next-gen GPU; we have an int4/FP8 path but you'll see slightly different latency profiles (int4 reduces memory, not always lower wall-clock latency depending on kernel). I'll note the kernel assumptions as a column in the next CSV.

2) Sample output (from mid-size candidate, prompt id P-17 from your prompt_set_v2):

> Prompt: "Extract entities and return canonical ticker mapping for: 'Acme Fin Services (ticker: ACFX), note: legacy name 'Acme FS' in some docs'"
> Response (mid-size model): "{\"entities\": [{\"name\": \"Acme Fin Services\", \"ticker\": \"ACFX\"}], \"confidence\": 0.92}"

Notes: we run an NER->normalization post-process that improves canonical mapping for ticker synonyms; raw hallucination cases were flagged in the CSV (column 'hallucination_flag').

3) Retention: 90-day logs with ingest redaction is supported in Redwood Private/Dedicated configs; for Hosted POC we can enable redaction and a 90-day TTL on indices — no problem. Marissa, can you confirm the SOC2/retention checklist?

Finally, agrees on adding a ticker slice — please send the list and we'll run a targeted regression test.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan@finlytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: technical qualification & model scorecard

Ethan — quick operational confirmation from Security & CS side: 

- PII redaction: we support token-level redaction at ingest. For the POC we'll provide a config snippet that redacts SSN and email patterns before logs persist.
- Retention: 90-day retention on logs is standard for Enterprise tenants; we'll provide the retention policy manifest and the audit log sample.
- Next steps / POC cadence: Sergio will draft a 2-week POC plan with routing rules (10% canary -> 50% ramp) and the three model variants we discussed (latency-first, balanced mid, distill batch). Karthik will drop an updated CSV with kernel assumptions and raw sample outputs.

Please reply with the ticker list and any additional slices you want us to score. If we get confirmation today we can spin up canary infra by Monday.

Cheers — Marissa
